fullText:
Summary: Swisstek (Ceylon) PLC (PARQ.N0000), the Lanka Tiles group's tile-grout and aluminium maker, has turned around strongly: EPS rose from a loss in 2023/24 to Rs 7.32 in 2025/26, and the six months to September 2026 were up another 8%. But at Rs 80.10 the share trades at 2.6x its NAV of Rs 31.06 and 10.6x trailing earnings, and the September quarter's profit fell 18% while borrowings jumped. Its profits are cyclical (losses in 2022/23 and 2023/24) and net debt is about 1.7x equity. Allowing today's 26% return on equity to fade, the methods put fair value at about Rs 46, so the price is about 74% above it. I'd buy at up to about Rs 39 and treat under Rs 34.50 as a strong buy.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 80.10 (Interim report to 30 Sep 2026 (closing price), 2026-09-30). Please check it live. In July–September 2026 it traded between Rs 67.10 and Rs 86.00. It closed the year to March 2026 at Rs 79.50, up from about Rs 47 a year earlier.
Six months to 30 September 2026 (group, unaudited): sales rose 8% to Rs 8.66bn and profit attributable rose 8% to Rs 418mn. EPS was Rs 3.05 against Rs 2.84. But the September quarter's EPS fell to Rs 1.44 from Rs 1.76, as administrative costs nearly doubled and finance costs rose.
Segments (six months): tile grout, adhesives and flooring sales rose 25% to Rs 2.60bn (profit before tax Rs 344mn); aluminium sales (Swisstek Aluminium) rose 2% to Rs 6.06bn (profit before tax Rs 318mn).
Year to March 2026 (audited): revenue Rs 16.88bn (up 11%), profit attributable Rs 1.00bn (up 16%), EPS Rs 7.32 (Rs 6.32), return on average equity 26%, dividends Rs 2.05 (28% of profit), NAV Rs 28.40.
Debt: borrowings Rs 9.16bn at September 2026, up from Rs 5.72bn in March, and net debt about Rs 8.6bn, about 1.7x equity. Operating cash flow was Rs 3.1bn negative in the half as stock rose and payables were paid down.
Cycle: group profit was Rs 900mn (2021/22), a loss of Rs 703mn (2022/23), a loss of Rs 113mn (2023/24, EPS Rs -0.51), then EPS Rs 6.32 (2024/25) and Rs 7.32 (2025/26).

Methods
NAV (Rs 31.06): 2.6x.
Return on equity: 26% in 2025/26 and 32% in 2024/25, after losses in the two years before.
P/E: 10.6x trailing EPS of Rs 7.53. Year-end P/E: 10.9x (2026), 7.4x (2025).
Dividends: Rs 2.05 for 2025/26, a 2.6% yield, 28% of profit.
Justified price to book: Rs 18.4 / 33.9 / 58.5, weighted Rs 34.2.
P/E method: Rs 39.6 / 60.0 / 80.0, weighted Rs 57.9.
Residual income: Rs 20.4 / 43.9 / 90.6, weighted Rs 46.2.

Swisstek pays out under a third of its profit, so a dividend model understates it, and its cash flow swings with aluminium stock, so a cash-flow DCF isn't reliable. Price to book is the strictest because it assumes ROE settles at 18% straight away; residual income lets today's ROE fade over 10 years.

Assumptions (bear / base / bull)
Cost of equity: 18.5% / 17% / 15.5% (a cyclical, highly geared manufacturer).
Long-run ROE (price to book): 13% / 18% / 23%.
ROE path (residual income): 20% falling to 13% / 24% falling to 18% / 26% falling to 23%.
Long-term growth: 5% / 6% / 7%.
EPS for the year to March 2027 × P/E: 6.6 × 6 / 7.5 × 8 / 8.0 × 10.
Average of the three methods: Rs 26.1 / Rs 45.9 / Rs 76.4.
Common: Sri Lankan 7–10-year government bonds yield about 12% (October 2026). The base case assumes the second half matches last year's Rs 4.48. Payout 28%.

Fair value and buy price
Fair value: weighting 30/50/20 gives about Rs 46 (1.5x NAV), so Rs 80.10 is about 74% above it.
Buy price: a 15% margin of safety gives Rs 39.10, and 25% gives Rs 34.50.
Plan for 500 shares: 200 at up to Rs 46.00, 150 at up to Rs 39.10 and 150 at up to Rs 34.50. That averages about Rs 40.48, about Rs 20,240, against Rs 40,050 at Rs 80.10.
Realism: Rs 46 needs about a 43% fall. The share was about Rs 47 in March 2025, so it was there recently, but it's unlikely soon while profits hold up.

Sensitivity (residual income base case, Rs per share)
Cost of equity 15.5%: 32.6 / 54.1 / 81.6 for long-run ROE of 13% / 18% / 23%.
Cost of equity 17%: 27.2 / 43.9 / 65.2.
Cost of equity 18.5%: 23.3 / 36.4 / 53.3.
Today's price needs ROE to stay above 23% for many years.

What would change my view
Supports a higher value: the tile-grout and flooring business keeps growing 25% a year; borrowings fall back as stock is sold; ROE stays above 25%; a building boom in Sri Lanka.
Supports a lower value: profit falling further after the weak September quarter; aluminium prices falling or price competition with Alumex; borrowings staying high; construction slowing; a return to the losses of 2022–2024.

These are my estimates from the annual reports for the years to March 2025 and March 2026 and the interim reports to June and September 2026. The interim figures are unaudited, so check the price before ordering. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.
